reaction.episode: DIGESTION episode through October 23 (data not stale): SPX 7,623.68, -2.82% off its 120-day high, -0.99% below its 50-day but +4.56% above its 200-day; SMH 527.20 between zones (-21.53% off high), NVDA 210.96 above Zone 1; VIX 19.45 with no rollover and HY OAS 3.23 calm; mechanical capitulation tally 1 of 4 (only credit-calm confirmed).
reaction.invalidation: A held SPX close above 7,820 with SMH above 600 and VIX rolling over would void the Watch stance — the digestion would be over, not deepening. Conversely, HY OAS above 4% or an SPX close below its 200-day (7,291.31) voids the 'contained' leg and turns the episode from digestion into distress, suspending the ladder.

ladder.response: Probe the Zone 2 tranche on the dislocation leaders (AVGO, ONTO, VRT); no full Add until a second low holds or a held close above the failure zone
ladder.trigger: SMH closes into Zone 2 (470-505) with the mechanical tally at 3 of 4

ladder.response: Probe only, small size — Zone 1 is the first shelf, not the bottom; wait for the second-low or failure-zone verdict before adding
ladder.trigger: SMH closes into Zone 1 (540-565) or NVDA closes into Zone 1 (200-210)

ladder.response: Treat as the trap case: do not chase, trim any probe adds made into the bounce, and wait for the retest verdict before re-entering
ladder.trigger: Bounce into the failure zone — SMH closes 580-600 or SPX closes 7,750-7,820 — then fails back below it

ladder.response: Stand down: no new probes, existing probes held not added, ladder suspended until credit calms and VIX rolls over
ladder.trigger: HY OAS closes above 4% or VIX closes above 25

ladder.response: Re-entry condition met: digestion ends on the upside verdict, or the Zone 2 breakdown completes and the second low becomes the new entry shelf — either way, entries only on confirmed closes, never on intraday spikes
ladder.trigger: Held SPX close above 7,820 with SMH above 600, or SMH closes below 470 and prints a holding second low

reaction.trapRisk: The October 21-23 failed retest already demonstrated the pattern: a close back below the 7,750-7,820 failure zone after touching it. Any bounce into SMH 580-600 or SPX 7,750-7,820 is presumed a bull trap until it holds for a close — entries happen only on zone closes or confirmed second lows, never into the first green bounce.

strategyPosture: Watch. The setup is rich — fundamentals ahead of price across AI silicon and selective power names — but no trigger has fired: SMH is between zones, NVDA is above Zone 1, and the capitulation tally is 1 of 4. Hold the zone ladder, do not chase the tape; new money stays in bills until a zone print plus tally confirmation, or a held reclaim of the failure zone, says otherwise.

themes.counterRead: Treating this as a confirmed broad rollover would misread the data: credit has not cracked and the index has not broken. But the divergence itself is real — TSLA is -25.4% off its high while AAPL is only -1.1% off — so position-level risk is much higher than index-level risk suggests. Size for the name, not the index.
themes.dataAnchor: The index itself is barely dented: SPY is -0.79% over the month and only -2.8% off its 52-week high, while the Mag 7 average sits -13.99% off highs — an 11.19-point divergence gap. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), and HY OAS is 3.23 and calm. The weakness is concentrated in the names that dominate the index, not in credit or in the broad market.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover: index calm masks concentrated weakness
themes.narrative: The tape reads like a broad unwind: QQQ is -4.89% over the month, VIX is up 24.12% over the month to 19.45, and the month's laggard board is a wall of red across AI, power, and nuclear names.
themes.watchFor: SLOOS or HY OAS turning: HY OAS closing above 4% would flip this theme from rotation to regime break.

themes.counterRead: DATA_AHEAD does not mean buy today: SMH sits BETWEEN_ZONES at 527.20, NVDA sits ABOVE_ZONE_1 at 210.96, and the mechanical capitulation tally is only 1 of 4. Fundamentals ahead of price is the setup, not the trigger — the trigger is zone occupancy, and neither name is in a zone yet.
themes.dataAnchor: The builders are still building. AVGO is -35% off its high while revenue grows 55% YoY with a 67.8% gross margin and 42.1% FCF margin; ONTO is -48.6% off its high with revenue +22.1% YoY; LRCX is -47.5% off its high with revenue +131.3% YoY; NVDA is only -13.3% off its high with revenue +61.4% YoY. AVGO (score 84, tier A), ONTO (81, tier A), and LRCX (79, tier B) lead the conviction board, and NVDA, AVGO, ONTO, and AMAT all sit on the watchlist-promotion list. The exception that proves the rule is AMAT: -49% off its high on just +11.4% revenue growth, flagged MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION — a derating, not a growth break.
themes.label: AI silicon dislocated: fundamentals building, prices falling
themes.narrative: The market is pricing AI infrastructure as a busted trade: SMH is -21.53% off its 120-day high and -13.08% over 20 days, and the semiconductor dislocation board reads like a capitulation list.
themes.watchFor: SMH closing into Zone 1 (540-565) or Zone 2 (470-505), or NVDA closing into Zone 1 (200-210).

themes.counterRead: Do not buy the theme; buy the split. BWXT's recovery profile earns a watchlist slot, VST's deteriorating revenue against insider buying is a warning, not a confirmation. The theme re-rates only when power demand shows up as contracted revenue, not as announcements.
themes.dataAnchor: The month's laggard board is the unwind: SMR -37.19%, OKLO -31.26%, URA -16.37%, GEV -14.87%, PWR -15.31%, CCJ -10.8%. Underneath, the split matters: BWXT is -47.4% off its high but revenue is growing 26.1% YoY (RECOVERY, watchlist promotion score 77), while VST — a holding — is -31.2% off its high with revenue DETERIORATING despite $1.17M of insider buying at the trough. The story was ahead of the contracts; the builders with real growth are now priced as if they had none.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: the story deflates faster than the build
themes.narrative: The power-for-AI story ran as a straight line: uranium, reactors, and grid suppliers priced as if every data-center announcement were already a signed contract.
themes.watchFor: BWXT or VST revenue inflection flipping to confirmed recovery, or SMR/OKLO stabilizing with a higher low after a zone print.

themes.counterRead: High rates explain the multiple compression in names like AMAT, but they do not explain a credit event that is not happening. If the FOMC decision lands without a credit crack, the digestion thesis holds and the zone ladder stays the plan; if HY OAS breaks 4%, the rates story stops being background and becomes the regime.
themes.dataAnchor: Rates are high but the curve is not inverted and credit is not stressed: 2-year 4.77%, 10-year 4.99%, 30-year 5.32%, 2s10s +0.22, real 10-year 2.64%, 10-year breakeven 2.35%, HY OAS 3.23 and calm, DFF 3.88%. SPX sits -0.99% below its 50-day and +4.56% above its 200-day — a digestion band, not a breakdown. The FOMC event (7 news hits, watch status) and the September CPI event (active) are the known catalysts, not hidden breaks. One honesty flag: this run's FRED feed came in PARTIAL, so rate prints are last-good cache where the feed failed, not fresh prints.
themes.label: Rates high, credit calm: digestion, not distress
themes.narrative: With the 10-year at 4.99% and the FOMC decision due October 27-28, the tape is braced for a hawkish surprise, and the rate level alone is treated as the reason equities cannot hold a bid.
themes.watchFor: FOMC decision October 28 and HY OAS closing above 4% or VIX closing above 25.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds at the zone edges, not in the middle: SMH drifting into Zone 1 (540-565) or down to Zone 2 (470-505), or NVDA closing into Zone 1 (200-210), is where the dislocation board converts into entries — and the FOMC decision on October 28 is the most likely trigger for the move in either direction.
